subject: physics
question_text: Distinguish between periodic motion and oscillatory motion. Give one example of each.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Periodic motion
lines: Periodic motion is any motion that repeats
itself in equal intervals of time.
Example: the motion of the earth around the sun.
steps.why: The only requirement is repetition after a fixed time; the path can be anything at all.
common_mistakes: Treating every periodic motion as a to-and-fro motion.

recall.must_convey: That periodic motion repeats itself in equal intervals of time.
accept: repeats in equal intervals of time
reject: to and fro about a mean position

steps.label: Oscillatory motion
lines: Oscillatory motion is periodic motion in which
the body moves to and fro about a fixed mean
but not all periodic motion is oscillatory.
steps.why: The earth going round the sun repeats but never turns back on itself — that is the whole difference.
common_mistakes: Saying the two words mean the same thing.

recall.must_convey: That oscillatory motion is to and fro about a mean position, so all oscillatory motion is periodic but not the reverse.
accept: to and fro about a mean position
reject: repeats in equal intervals of time
